newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Timing of Japan interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Timing of Japan interest rate rise.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Deputy Governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted by an executive of a labour group on Wednesday as saying the central bank was considering the right timing to raise its official discount rate but that the central bank did not want to make a hasty decision. The remark caused Tokyo stocks to fall, Japanese government bonds to sink and the dollar to dip briefly on speculation that the central bank might be willing to raise its rock-bottom interest rates sooner rather than later.
TOSHIKINI KANEKI, ECONOMIST, SUMITOMO TRUST AND BANKING

"It is not the time yet to raise rates. I think you can say chances that the Bank of Japan might stop guiding money market rates lower have increased. If that happens it would happen sometime in July after the next tankan (BOJ's quarterly corporate survey). While the chances of this have increased, the situation is not such that the BOJ must stop guiding money market rates lower."
MICHAEL HARTNETT, SENIOR ECONOMIST, MERRILL LYNCH

"The yen's rise obviates the need for the BOJ to raise rates in the near future. The yen's rise does a number of things for the authorities. If the yen fell to 135 yen as it had been threatening to do so a little while ago then they would have had to raise rates to protect the yen. The move in the bond market and the yen relieves three pressures -- trade pressure from the U.S., pressure to raise interest rates and makes institutional investors worried enough to help stop the capital outflow taking place."
MINEKO SASAKI-SMITH, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CS FIRST BOSTON
"I think they (BOJ) are preparing themselves so that if they are told (by politicians) to raise rates, they don't look silly, but a rate hike is by no means assured.

"It was only on Monday that (BOJ research director Masayuki) Matsushima said the impact of the consumption tax hike would last three months, which gives the impression that they want to ensure the impact has disappeared before acting."
YASUHIKO USHIKUBO, ECONOMIST AT INDUSTRIAL BANK OF JAPAN

"I don't think there was any deep meaning to the BOJ deputy governor's quoted comments. The BOJ will be watching the overall economic conditions and then make a judgement. They'll raise interest rates when the time comes, but Fukui's comments did not indicate the timing of the hike.

"Had the comments been made around January or February, they probably would have been ignored. There will be some overreaction to comments that can be taken as hinting of a rise in interest rates for a while.
"Markets will realise the economy is not doing so well in April to June period and realise they will have to wait until the next tankan survey expected out in July. Then they will settle down."
Ushikubo added that a BOJ rate hike was unlikely until the October to December quarter.
KENJI ARATA, ECONOMIST, MCM ASIA PACIFIC

"It is quite possible that rates will be raised but it is a question of timing. The BOJ still needs time to evaluate the effect of factors such as the rise in the sales tax, the stop to the special income taxes and the increase in health insurance costs.

"So the BOJ will have to wait for at least the all the indicators for the April to June quarter to come out first. I think it is possible that there will be a stop to the BOJ's policy of guiding money market rates lower in August if it becomes clear that private demand is not threatened. Then I think there may be a possibility of a rise in the official discount rate in September."
